There's a bug that shows the rate limit modal even after logging in. 
### Steps to Reproduce
1. get rate limited as not logged in user. 
2. press the login with github button
3. page automatically reloads with you signed in, but the rate limit modal still appears
at this step we would just refresh and it works fine, but I fear that this may not be intuitive for new users.
### Fix
Please make sure that the page waits to see if you're logged in before displaying the rate limit modal.
Notice: you can get rate limited while logged in so also make sure that this is handled.

What is this? There should always be documentation around environment variables, ideally in the README; as this affects setup and the ability for others to work on this. 
Although I don't see why a new env var is necessary in the first place.

Can't this be wrapped within an `expect toThrow` check?

I believe the mock just needs to be updated with the proper ID. Everything there is mocked so everything is controlled and never reaches the real endpoints. Should be a very minor change fitting in this pull request.
I can give a look later. But if that is the only way, make sure to reset this so we don't silence all the errors from the tests, only this specific one.

I think this should be removed, as well as the `throw` inside the function `getNewSessionToken`. We should not make the page crash only because we could not retrieve the token, a `console.error` should suffice.

I believe it would be this one https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/pull/35
Let's merge it first so you can rebase and make sure everything works as expected.
Is there no better check that this? If one letter in the text changes it breaks the whole login. Also `500` and `server_error` seem pretty redundant.

I mean that the only check here should be `code === '500'`. `err` is just the translation of the `code` to readable text, and `desc` just sent by Supabase as a default error message.
You can use it to output the error instead:
`console.error(desc);`
Shouldn't `(!user)` be enough for this check?

Instead of checking the error message string, I think it might be wiser to call https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v20#rate-limit which seems to be there for this purpose?
If it works fine, the same principle can be applied on line 34.
Any reason for this export? I do not see it called anywhere in the content of this pull request.
Does this take the UTC into account when displayed?
This displays a TypeScript error as `error` is `unknown`

While I am not against the idea, I think it is better to check the type with `instanceof` and use the Octokit provided [error library](https://github.com/octokit/request-error.js?tab=readme-ov-file#usage-with-octokit) to avoid recreating an error within the catch blocks

It does but afaik it only works with username, not the user id
https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v20#users-get-by-username
Using request seems to be the only way

The rate limited cases can be very easily simulated within Cypress by intercepting routes and sending back the appropriate response. It should help you develop and test these cases without having to really spam the endpoint. Also, would be nice to see these testing cases implemented.

There are JSON example responses in the docs, they don't include failed cases but for each route you have the return codes, which I believe should suffice. That would be really great to have some test for sure!
